text:
alex: Heads-up — I ran the Q4 hosted GPU forward curve with the new customer growth model and there's a potential ~18% shortfall vs committed reservations in eu-west by mid-November.

mira: Can you paste the numbers? rough is fine.

alex: Sure. rough numbers: hosted peak tokens/day -> 1.9T, capacity need ~420 A100-equivalent GPUs. Committed supply (current reservations + planned buys) -> 345 GPUs. gap ~75 GPUs (~18%).

sam: Oof. Is that peak or sustained? burstable?

alex: Peak (95th percentile over rolling 7d). sustained 7d avg gap is ~40 GPUs. We assume current batching & prefix cache levels.

jin: Region breakdown? sounds eu-heavy.

alex: eu-west: gap 48 GPUs. us-west: gap 20 GPUs. ap-south: small surplus (we're overcommitted by ~5 there).

capacity-bot: [automated] Forecast run completed 2026-03-17. Sensitivity scenarios: +/-10% demand, +/-5% autoscale effectiveness. See /s3/infra/forecasts/2283056789.csv

mira: Is the gap a hard deficit (we run out) or a perf degradation risk?

alex: Likely graceful degradation: increased queueing for some low-tier requests and fallback to smaller model variants for heavy workloads. But SLA risk if two large customers spike simultaneously.

nina: What's the billing picture? are committed discounts still favorable vs on-demand?

alex: Yes — committed reservations still 30-40% cheaper per-hour than on-demand for our vendor. But buying extra commitment increases our fixed cost. Current expected utilization of new reservations is ~78% in the baseline.

sam: Did you run a sensitivity where we tweak batching/caching? how much headroom?

alex: Yes. Improving batching by +15% reduces GPU need by ~22 GPUs. Enabling more aggressive KV prefix caching on 3 heavy routes buys ~12 GPUs equivalent. Total ~34 GPUs if we do both.

jin: So we can close ~45% of the gap with infra changes. Remaining ~30 GPUs still a decision.

mira: Can we rezone some traffic from eu-west to us-west during EU non-peak hours to smooth? any latency/SLA constraints?

alex: We have a routing policy that prefers regional serving for latency-sensitive routes. For non-latency routes (batch embeddings, retraining), we can shift. Real-time chat will suffer. Estimated shiftable load ~8 GPUs equivalent.

nina: Another lever: short-term reserved commitments (3mo) vs 1yr? vendors offer 3mo with smaller discount. Could buy bridge commitments.
sam: What's the cost math for 3mo bridging vs paying on-demand + risk of unused capacity?
alex: Quick calc: 3mo reserved cost for 30 GPUs ~ $X (we should attach sheet), still cheaper than on-demand even if 30% unused. Break-even if utilization falls < 12%.

mira: Any billing anomalies? I remember we had an overstated committed usage last month.

alex: I dug in — there was a tagging issue where archived test clusters were still counted against our committed pool for 72h. Fixed. That improved effective free capacity by ~3 GPUs historically but not enough.

capacity-bot: [note] Recent billing alert: unused-commitment-threshold at 20% reached for ap-south 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-11.

jin: Actionable plan proposals: 1) Short-term: enable batching & caching improvements (owner: eng-runtime @sam, ETA 10d). 2) Medium-term: purchase 3mo bridge for 25 GPUs for eu-west (owner: finance + infra @nina, decision in 3d). 3) Traffic smoothing policies for non-RT routes (owner: eng-platform @jin, ETA 7d). 4) Long-term: prioritize model quantization A/B on heavy routes (owner: eng-ml @mira).

sam: A few notes — runtime changes are low-risk; I can prod a staged rollout and measure token-per-second improvements. I'll post perf numbers to this thread.

nina: I'll run the cost calc + vendor terms and propose purchase options tomorrow. We should include early termination clauses.

alex: I'll update the forecast with post-batching assumptions and rerun the sensitivity.

mira: If we decide to buy 25 GPUs 3mo, is procurement fast enough?
nina: Yes, for short-term bridge we can spin them up in 48-72h after PO, pushing to vendor priority queue might shave time.

sam: quick question — any impact on Dedicated customers? we shouldn't cannibalize reserved pools.

alex: Dedicated pools are isolated. This is hosted API pool only. But cross-checking capacity quotas with Dedicated ops is on the checklist.

jin: Add a monitoring alert to watch eu-west queue wait time and model-fallback rate. Threshold: queue > 150ms p50 for 5m or fallback > 0.5% over 15m -> page oncall.

mira: Good. Also add a cost delta alert if projected monthly committed spend increases >10% from baseline.

capacity-bot: [task created] infra/ops#452: Run enhanced forecast + batch/caching toggles. assigned to alex, sam, nina. due 2026-03-20.

alex: Thanks — will sync with @mira tomorrow 10:30.

nina: thumbs for plan. :+1:

sam: I'll start a feature branch for the batching tuning and post perf dumps.

mira: Let's reconvene after the perf numbers. If worst-case holds and remaining gap >20 GPUs, recommend approving 3mo bridge.

alex: Agreed.

jin: Closing notes: we should also add short doc for CS about potential degraded behaviors so they can prep customer comms.

mira: I'll draft a blunt one-pager: "What to expect if hosted capacity tightens".

alex: End of thread for now. Thanks all.
